public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 922

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/922](https://www.erdosproblems.com/922)
- [ErHa67b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, András, *On chromatic graphs*. Mat. Lapok (1967), 1-4.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [Fo70b] Folkman, J. H., *An upper bound on the chromatic number of a graph*. (1970), 437-457.
-/

@[expose] public section

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos922

/--
Let $k\geq 0$. Let $G$ be a graph such that every subgraph $H$ contains an independent set of size
$\geq (n-k)/2$, where $n$ is the number of vertices of $H$. Must $G$ have chromatic number at most
$k+2$?

A question of Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa67b]. The case $k=0$ is trivial, but they could not prove
this even for $k=1$.

This is true, and was proved by Folkman [Fo70b].

See also [73](https://www.erdosproblems.com/73).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos922.lean#L5595"]
theorem erdos_922 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
    (∀ S : Finset V, ∃ I : Finset V, I ⊆ S ∧ (G.induce (I : Set V)).edgeSet = ∅ ∧
      (I.card : ℝ) ≥ (S.card - k : ℝ) / 2) →
    G.chromaticNumber ≤ k + 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos922

reformulations.difference: Lean restricts to finite vertex types and tests vertex finsets, expressing independence by an empty edge set of the induced graph. The source speaks of every subgraph, and the original papers also allow arbitrary graphs tested on finite vertex sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An induced graph on I has empty edge set exactly when I is independent. Testing induced subgraphs suffices: deleting edges preserves independence, while induced subgraphs are themselves subgraphs. The numerical condition is exactly |S| ≤ 2|I| + k, with real subtraction and division rather than truncated natural arithmetic. For arbitrary G, the hypothesis passes to every finite subgraph. The finite statement makes each such subgraph (k+2)-colorable, and de Bruijn–Erdős compactness gives a coloring of G; the converse follows by specialization to finite graphs. The complete equivalence is proved as Review922.finite_statement_iff_original in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the problem's sorry-backed theorem.

The exact linked external proof compiled successfully; a separately compiled adapter also derives the exact repository statement. Both depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
